appendix_source_diff: The five origins are January 23, November 12 and December 21, 2021, and May 11 and December 25, 2022. Nine Bayesian variants combine Gaussian (N), asymmetric Laplace (AL) or extended asymmetric Laplace (exAL) likelihoods with gauge-only (U) or source-inclusive (M) observations and transfer-active (T1) or forecast-transfer-suppressed (T0) configurations. M-T0 retains transfer during historical fitting. AL/exAL predictive syntheses combine fits at probabilities $0.05,0.20,0.35,0.50,0.65,0.80,0.95$. The exAL-M-T1 configuration is the reference specification.

-Table~\ref{tab:crps_all_origins} gives mean continuous ranked probability scores (CRPS; smaller is better) using the reported quantile-grid calculation on transformed discharge. External references are raw GloFAS/NWS ensembles, seasonal climatology, persistence and GloFAS ensemble model output statistics (EMOS). The horizons retain matching verification dates, with NWS available only for eight days. Aggregate means and climatology-relative skill appear in the main paper.

-Table~\ref{tab:quantile_check_loss} reports check losses for each origin and target probability; the pooled 28-day comparison is in the main paper. These are losses of synthesized predictive quantiles against subsequent USGS observations, not losses of conditional model locations. Tables~\ref{tab:exact_score_sensitivity} and \ref{tab:discharge_scale_scores} distinguish exact empirical-distribution scores, the independent-draw sensitivity and discharge-scale results. Subsection~\ref{app:numericalprediction} defines their finite-representation conventions. Table~\ref{tab:origin_interval_coverage} reports the origin-specific central 95\% interval counts. The analysis materials also provide complete reliability hits, ties, interval scores and raw-product error/spread summaries \citep{deleon2026sanlorenzo_reproducibility}.

-The main paper's quantile-grid score equals the exact score plus $D/[m^2(m+1)]$, explaining their difference on the same predictive values \citep{zamo2018crps}. The adjusted score estimates the parent-distribution CRPS under independent, identically distributed draws \citep{ferro2014fair}; that assumption is additional for physical ensembles. The adjustment is inapplicable to deterministic quantile grids and point masses. Exact skill uses the matching exact climatology denominator; no adjusted skill is reported.

-For each lead, the EMOS fit minimizes the analytic truncated-normal CRPS over the eligible training cases described in the main paper. We use four deterministic initial values and bounded limited-memory Broyden--Fletcher--Goldfarb--Shanno optimization (L-BFGS-B), retaining the converged solution with the lowest objective. The constraints are \(b,d\geq0\) and \(c>0\) in the location and variance parameterization. Training cases, numerical scaling and bounds, fitted parameter values, convergence criteria and boundary assessments are included in the reproducibility materials.

For target probability $p_0$, $\operatorname{exAL}_{p_0}(\mu,\sigma,\gamma)$ denotes the extended asymmetric Laplace working likelihood with quantile location $\mu$, scale $\sigma>0$ and skewness $\gamma$ in the domain defined below. Each quantile model uses a shared $p$-dimensional trend/seasonal state $\boldsymbol\theta_t$, source discrepancies $\boldsymbol\delta_t^j$ and an $(m+1)$-dimensional transfer block. Let $\mathcal J=\{1,\ldots,J\}$ index external sources; source $j$ has members $i\in\mathcal I_j=\{1,\ldots,I_j\}$ and leads $k\in\mathcal K_j=\{1,\ldots,K_{(j)}\}$, with $K_{\max}=\max_jK_{(j)}$. Algorithms~\ref{alg:Alg3} and \ref{alg:Alg4} display historical-window coordinate updates and Gaussian state recursions. Initialize state moments from $\mathcal N(\mathbf m_0,\mathbf C_0)$ and initialize augmentation and channel-parameter moments before the first outer iteration. Angle brackets denote expectations under the current variational factors; $\mathcal L$ denotes the evidence lower bound (ELBO). The same observation-level updates apply to each available forecast member after replacing $(t,j)$ by $(T+k,j,i)$ and using the corresponding selector and active-state transition. In the forecast window, an observation vector stacks all active pairs \((j,i)\), where \(j\) identifies a source and \(i\) a member. Selector columns repeat within a source, while each member has its own augmentation variables. A source-specific parameter objective includes every retrospective value and available issued member: with complete historical support this gives \(T+I_jK_{(j)}\) contributions for external source \(j\), and \(T\) for the gauge channel. Forecast state evolution uses the covariance specification in Subsection~\ref{app:forecastcovariance}.
